title: Law of Sines and Law of Cosines

questions.q: Two observers 400 m apart on a straight road both sight a hot-air balloon between them. The angles of elevation are $58°$ and $47°$. Find the distance from the balloon to the first observer (the one with the $58°$ sighting), to the nearest metre.
questions.answer: The angle at the balloon is $180° - 58° - 47° = 75°$. By the Law of Sines, $d = \frac{400\sin 47°}{\sin 75°} \approx 303$ m.

questions.q: In triangle $PQR$, two sides of length 8 and 11 enclose an angle of $52°$. Find the length of the third side, to two decimal places.
A triangle has sides 7, 9, and 12. Find the measure of its largest angle, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
questions.answer: The largest angle is opposite the side of length 12: $\cos C = \frac{7^2 + 9^2 - 12^2}{2(7)(9)} = \frac{-14}{126} = -\frac{1}{9}$, so $C \approx 96.4°$.

questions.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 10 and 14 enclosing an angle of $35°$, to two decimal places.
A ship sails 30 km due east, then turns and sails 45 km on a bearing of $N \, 50° \, E$. Decide which law applies and find the ship's distance from its starting point, to the nearest kilometre.
questions.answer: The angle between the legs is $90° + 50° = 140°$. Law of Cosines: $d^2 = 30^2 + 45^2 - 2(30)(45)\cos 140° \approx 2925 + 2068.4 = 4993.4$, so $d \approx 71$ km.

questions.q: In triangle $ABC$, $A = 30°$, $a = 5$, and $b = 9$. Determine how many triangles satisfy these conditions (zero, one, or two), and find all possible measures of angle $B$.
questions.answer: $\sin B = \frac{b\sin A}{a} = \frac{9(0.5)}{5} = 0.9$. This gives $B \approx 64.2°$ or $B \approx 115.8°$. Since $A + B < 180°$ in both cases, there are two possible triangles.

questions.q: In triangle $DEF$, $D = 40°$, $d = 10$, and $e = 6$. Determine how many triangles satisfy these conditions, explaining your reasoning.
questions.answer: $\sin E = \frac{e\sin D}{d} = \frac{6\sin 40°}{10} \approx 0.386$, giving $E \approx 22.7°$ or $E \approx 157.3°$. Since $d > e$ (the side opposite the given angle is longer), only the acute solution is valid: exactly one triangle exists.

questions.q: For each triangle description, state whether the Law of Sines or the Law of Cosines is the appropriate first tool, and why:
parts: Two angles and one side are known (AAS).
Two sides and the included angle are known (SAS).
answers: Law of Sines — a full angle-side ratio pair is available.
Law of Cosines — no angle is known to pair with a side.
Law of Cosines — the included angle lets you find the third side directly.

questions.q: A triangular plot of land has sides 120 m, 150 m, and 90 m. Find its area, to the nearest square metre, using the fact that you can first find any angle with the Law of Cosines and then use $A = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$.
questions.answer: Find angle $C$ between the sides of length 120 and 150 (opposite the side 90): $\cos C = \frac{120^2+150^2-90^2}{2(120)(150)} = \frac{28800}{36000}=0.8$, so $C \approx 36.87°$. Area $=\frac{1}{2}(120)(150)\sin(36.87°) \approx 9000(0.6) = 5400$ m$^2$.
